newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy 1997-98 PSBR seen in line for EMU - bankers.
newsitem.headline: Italy 1997-98 PSBR seen in line for EMU - bankers.

text.p: Italy has made great progress in overhauling state finances in line with Maastricht criteria and its state sector borrowing needs for 1997-1998 will be on target for the single European currency, the Italian Banking Association (ABI) said.
ABI said in its latest Financial Outlook that 1997 PSBR was seen at 59 trillion lire and at 61 trillion in 1998.
It forecast Gross domestic product (GDP) growth at 1.1 percent this year and 2.2 percent for 1998.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government has targeted a 1997 budget deficit of 58.7 trillion lire, or 3.0 percent of GDP, and of 56.9 trillion lire in 1998, or 2.8 percent of GDP. The targets take account of supplementary deficit-cutting measures.
The government forecasts GDP growth of 1.2 percent this year and of 2.0 percent in 1998.
The ABI report said the cost of such efforts "is the modest cyclical profile of the Italian economy."
It saw private consumer demand growing 0.7 percent this year accelerating to 1.6 percent in 1998.
Growth in gross fixed investments was seen jumping to 5.0 percent next year from 1.7 percent this year.

ABI said that indications from bank analysts contributing to the report "reflect a consensus scenario which sees Italy achieving the macroeconomic parameters set for joining the single European currency."
"However, the issue of Italy's entry into the euro from the start has to be left to the interpretation of these parameters to be made in mid-1998," the report added.
